answer: The design leans on receipt hashes checked against public logs before trust. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ember of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The mirror lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the nadir is where a second reviewer recomputes them. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
